title: Sort
description: A summer photograph of a level crossing with one wave of it pixel-sorted: the verge is combed into solid horizontal strips, and up the curl the grass is lifted in long sorted rows that climb from the ground and arch over the crossing, each strip ramping from dark green at its root to a bright tail, thinning as it rises, with a few white-gold glints breaking off at the crest, while every pole and sign at the verge stays untouched. Brush anywhere and the picture sorts under your hand, live on the GPU; the longer and harder you brush, the longer the spans grow and the further the rows are stretched up the curl. Press and hold and the sort runs backwards, every pixel sliding home.
intent: After Kim Asendorf's ASDF Pixel Sort (2010, https://github.com/kimasendorf/ASDFPixelSort) and herb's generative reference 2 (a street photo smeared into horizontal strips that curl up like grass). The print's 2400x1600 is cut into bands 8-14 px tall; each is sorted once along its centre row and that row is written down the whole band, so every run is a solid rectangle. Spans may only start on grass and run on, within a reach and an ASDF luminance interval that both grow with the brush, ending once they have run 30% of their reach through anything but vegetation, or at a silhouette in the depth map (Depth Anything V2) or a depth step, so they never cross a pole; sorted by luminance pulled down by greenness, so each run is one ramp from dark green to its brightest pixels, by odd-even transposition in WebGL2 fragment passes; outside a span the same network orders pixels by home index, so erasing the mask sorts every pixel back home. The wave is geometry: up the curl the print is cut into its own stripes, about 14 px at the verge thinning to 2-3 px at the crest with hairlines among them, and each stripe shows one long sorted verge run picked by its radius, stretched across the envelope with its gradient kept and read through a short window along the run, its tail stopping short by a hashed amount so the edge combs like grass; a handful of bright tails near the crest break off as glint tiles.

sources.author: XS Xue (@xxs11)
sources.note: 6000x4000 original, shown at 2400x1600; depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py, 1200x800.
